focus.$description: Keyboard focus-indicator ring. INFERRED standard — the HSBC Common Toolkit Figma library carries NO canonical focus primitive (searched 2026-06-19: no focus/outline/ring variable exists; focus is handled in the React/CSS layer, not as a token). Grounded in the system's existing information-blue ramp rather than an invented hex. SIGNED OFF as canon by Dave 2026-06-20 (was tagged review). Ring width/offset live in layout.json (focus block). Standard: guidelines/focus-indicators.md. Contrast verified ≥3:1 (1.4.11): light 7.17:1 on #FFFFFF, dark 4.24:1 on #1D1D1D.

button.$description: DEDICATED button-ladder tokens (Dave, 2026-07-19: 'look at the tokens in the canon for inspiration' — mirrors the surface/secondary/tertiary DTCG shape). Apollo Mono's button ladder is secondary (grey filled) / tertiary (outline) / quaternary (undecorated text) — there is NO button/primary here: red primary is Apollo LEGACY only, parked. Added as a NEW group rather than recolouring the existing secondary/* and tertiary/* tokens, which are OVERLOADED: secondary/background is also the checkbox/radio/tab-bar CHECKED fill, and tertiary/background is SURFACES (aliased to surface/raised, used by cards/modals/panels/slider). Recolouring either would have broken those other consumers. All values a11y-verified and ruled by Dave — do not invent, round, or adjust. 2026-07-20: re-pointed onto the semantic middle layer (surface/action*, text/on-action, border/action-strong) so button/* is a proper three-tier stack (component → semantic → primitive, _STANDARDS.md §1) instead of aliasing primitives directly. Non-disabled resolved values are UNCHANGED by this pass. Disabled leaves (contrast-exempt per WCAG spec) were re-pointed onto the pre-existing text/disabled and border/subtle semantics and now carry those semantics' resolved values — a small, deliberate value shift on 4 disabled leaves only; see notes on each.

state.note: Default ground = solid colour (universal substrate). Per ADR-0009, mechanism is a per-theme SET {colour|opacity|both}; chromatic themes supply a distinct hue via their override set.

Mono hover renders via OPACITY (fill fades over background/default at this alpha). The colour $value is the ramp-snapped opaque EQUIVALENT, stored for colour-only consumers/adapters. A chromatic theme instead sets mechanism:[colour] with a distinct hue; a theme may set both. Per ADR-0009. Opacity migrates to a first-class number/opacity token with the style-builder + snippet rebind.
Pressed ground = solid colour. Mechanism selectable per ADR-0009.

digital-black.$name: digital black (Dave 2026-07-18: "it can be called digital black or something, that's probably how I'll remember it")
digital-black.$note: derived (no primitive alias) — the DIGITAL SUBSTITUTE for the brand black #000000 (color/black). ⚠️ CONDITIONAL, not a free second black: use ONLY where light/reverse text sits ON the dark ground. Pure black remains brand-canon and stays correct for borders, marks, rules and any surface carrying no reverse text. RATIONALE: #000 maximises the luminance step against white (21:1), which drives halation — the bright field blooming across the edge, read as text that 'dances'. #1A1A1A cuts that step ~17% to 17.4:1 and settles the text without reducing legibility. The NAME deliberately favours recall over precision (Dave's call, he is the one who must remember it) — it does NOT encode the condition, so the condition lives here and must travel with it.
digital-black.$condition: light or reverse text sits on this ground
digital-black.$rule: reduce the extremity of the edge — the NEUTRAL-ground lever. Its coloured-ground twin is the saturation ceiling (≤0.72). Both reduce edge extremity; neither adds contrast, which makes halation worse.
digital-black.$provenance: in production use since ~2026-07-04 via _PROFORMA-RULES.md rule 1 (Apollo mono primary), but until 2026-07-18 it existed ONLY as prose — no token, no gate, rationale unrecorded. Promoted on Dave's ruling 2026-07-18. Holding-pen record: tokens/_proposals/neutral-blacks.proposals.json
